text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert: eu-west-2 router p99 > 1.5s for streaming/generate endpoints. Triggered at 2026-03-15T01:12:02Z. Paging on-call. Links: https://dash.redwood/internal/slo/euw2 | logs: https://logs.redwood/euw2/streams/1769804322

maya: I'm on it, taking primary. seeing p95 jump too ~600ms and p99 at 1.8s. Streaming stalls correlate with certain upstream shards. :eyes:

sam: noticed a routing policy rollout 01:05 that bumped weight for new redispatch rule in eu-west-2. could be related. rolling history: `router-policy-2026-03-15-0105`

lee: adding context: we have alerts for increased queue depth on lb-proxy instances in euw2-a and euw2-b, but not euw2-c. Hot partitions on shard keys from a small subset of customers.

cassie: customer-impact check: support-queue shows ~18 customer sessions reporting streaming stalls, 2 raised SEV. juli, can you confirm numbers?

julian: support: confirmed ~18 customers affected, estimates: 3% of total requests in region delayed >1s, 0.6% errors (stream disconnect). we have 2 enterprise customers on the line asking for status.

maya: immediate mitigations: 1) pause recent router policy rollout; 2) enable eager-fallback to fallback-model for streaming paths for requests hitting hot shards; 3) throttle request concurrency from problematic prefixes. Running commands now.

sam: rollback command issued: `rbctl policies rollback router-policy-2026-03-15-0105 --region eu-west-2`

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Rollback started by sam at 2026-03-15T01:16:23Z. CI checks OK; applying to eu-west-2.

lee: while rollback applies, toggled eager-fallback: `PATCH /config/routers/euw2` payload `{ "eager_fallback": true, "fallback_model": "gen-small" }`

cassie: throttle applied to hot prefixes: `trafficctl set-rate --prefix sh-42 --qps 50 --region euw2`

maya: rebalancing suggestion: temporarily exclude hot shard from normal hash affinity so traffic fans out across more routers. Will open a short window to rebalance.

sam: quick check of logs shows misrouting probability spike matching the rollout window. snippets: ```[01:06:10Z] route_eval: chose redispatch-v2 over local-affinity (weight 0.7) [01:06:12Z] queue: depth increased node=lb-7 size=246```

lee: observed memory pressure on a subset of routers from sticky KV-caches; redispatch to larger hosts caused uneven KV cache misses -> regen of KV for many requests -> tail. Might be interplay between redispatch weight and caching.

natalie: FYI I'm updating status page and posting to #customer-notify. Draft: "We are investigating increased latency in EU-West-2 streaming endpoints. Mitigations underway; some customers may experience brief stalls." :thumbsup:

julian: support: notifying the two SEV accounts now with interim mitigation details and ETA ~20m for stabilization.

ops-bot: rollback finished at 2026-03-15T01:21:05Z. Changes applied to eu-west-2.

maya: seeing p99 down to ~1.1s, p95 ~420ms. Not back to baseline yet but improving. continuing rebalancing and KV-cache warm-up.

sam: can we kick a controlled shard-reshuffle to move hot keys off overloaded routers? command: `routerctl reshuffle --shard sh-42 --target-policy spread --region euw2 --duration 5m`

lee: initiating reshuffle. note: reshuffle increases transient CPU/memory; will monitor.

cassie: while reshuffle runs, enable slight autoscale on lb-proxy pool (scale +2) to absorb queue. `autoscale set lb-proxy-euw2 min=4 max=8`

maya: handoff: I'm going to the bridge, leaving sam as primary for next 30m. ping sam for questions. :ringer:

sam: ack. I'll continue triage and coordinate with runtime to ensure no regressions of policy rollouts.

julian: update to customers: sent message to affected accounts with steps we took and that we're monitoring. No full data loss, mostly stalls and disconnects for streaming sessions.

natalie: status page updated: "Partial latency degradation in EU-West-2; mitigations in progress. We will provide updates every 10 minutes."

ops-bot: metric-check: p99 00m 30s post-rollback = 980ms. p95 = 360ms. error-rate trending down.

maya: next actions: 1) monitor until p99 < 700ms for 10m; 2) run postmortem to capture policy rollout safeguards and add canary for redispatch weight changes; 3) Q: do we need an immediate rollback of other policy rollouts? sam please check global rollout queue.

sam: checking: no other similar rollouts in flight. I'll add a safety flag to block redispatch weight changes without a slow canary.

cassie: raising incident classification to SEV-2 (customer-impacting latency) and scheduling postmortem. tagging oncall and product for follow-up. :heavy_exclamation_mark:

julian: any ETA for closing the page? once p99 stable and customers confirmed, will coordinate communications and close.

maya: will monitor for 30m; if stable will close and join postmortem. Thanks team. :heart:
